Item 8.01 Other Events.
In connection with recent lawsuits filed by various shareholders in the Court of Chancery in Delaware, which have been consolidated under the action captioned 
In Re Meta Platforms, Inc. Class C Reclassification Litigation, Consol.
 C.A. No. 2026-1413-KSJM (the “Shareholder Litigation”), asserting claims challenging the recapitalization of Meta Platforms, Inc. (the “Company”) with a trial scheduled to begin April 19, 2027, the Company has agreed that it will not issue any shares of Class C common stock, whether through a dividend or otherwise, during the pendency of the pre-trial and trial proceedings in the Court of Chancery. 
In furtherance of this, Mark Zuckerberg, the Company’s founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer, granted a waiver to the Company of the requirement in the Founder Alignment Agreement, dated October 20, 2026, between the Company and Mr. Zuckerberg, that the dividend of Class C common stock previously declared by the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Stock Dividend”) be paid by no later than the fifth business day following the effectiveness of the Company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation. Such waiver will expire on the earlier of (i) the Company’s failure to pay the Stock Dividend within a reasonable period following resolution of the Shareholder Litigation that does not prohibit or enjoin the payment of the Stock Dividend; (ii) a final, non-appealable resolution of the Shareholder Litigation that prohibits or enjoins the payment of the Stock Dividend; and (iii) June 30, 2027, if the Stock Dividend has not been paid on or prior to such date. Because the Company will not launch its previously announced at-the-market program until the Class C common stock begins trading, it does not expect to launch the at-the-market program until after the Stock Dividend is paid.
